name: Western Australia
summary: A British blue ensign with a yellow disc in the fly bearing a black swan. The swan was turned to face the hoist in 1953.
origin: The black swan has represented Western Australia since the Swan River Colony was founded in 1829. The flag dates from 1870; in 1953 the swan was redrawn facing the hoist, as heraldic animals traditionally do.

symbols.name: Black swan
symbols.description: A black swan swimming toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: The state's emblem and its first colony on the Swan River.

facts: Black swans are native to Australia; Europeans long assumed all swans were white.
Perth lies on the Swan River.
Western Australia is the largest Australian state.
clues: A blue ensign with a black swan on a yellow disc.
Its swan was turned around in 1953.
Its capital lies on a river named after the bird.
